limits.error: none; the translated query is the same text under either setting, except a keep before an unwrap and a function taken per series after a parser with no keep or after an extraction list, whose series follow Loki only with the lowering on. A lowering that panics is recovered, counted as `panic` and answered by the string translator
limits.metric: loki_vl_proxy_lowering_shadow_total{result="flipped",construct="LogSelect"}, and the same counter with construct UnwrapKeepIdentity for a keep before an unwrap and UnwrapDynamicIdentity for a function taken per series after a parser
limits.sizing: On is the default: the lowering writes the string translator's text byte for byte on the whole query corpus under every translator profile (a CI gate), takes less CPU and fewer bytes per translation than the translator on the shapes it covers, and only runs on a translation cache miss. A query it does not cover (a metric query, a parser or formatting stage, a detected_level or service_name filter) is decided by a scan of its text and not planned. Turn it off (false) as a rollback if a translated query ever differs from the string translator's: compare -translate-shadow-sample=1 with it off to see the difference as mismatch counts by construct.

limits.bounds: loki (the default) or victorialogs: how the data.stats object of query, query_range, volume and volume_range answers is filled. Nothing grows with the setting: the stats object is a fixed-size rendering per answer, and Loki's accounting reads only the answer, the request and the volume answers the proxy already keeps
limits.error: none; an unknown value stops the proxy at start-up with `invalid -query-stats-mode`
limits.loki_parity: data.stats of Loki's query, query_range and index/volume answers
limits.sizing: loki is the default: Grafana's query inspector and the Logs Drilldown footer show numbers close to Loki's for the same query (estimated where VictoriaLogs does not tell them, documented per field in the API reference). Set victorialogs to see what the proxy actually read from VictoriaLogs for each request, for example when sizing VictoriaLogs or comparing the proxy's own work across replicas.

limits.bounds: false (the default) estimates a metric query's bytes processed from the selector's mean line size; true reads them from VictoriaLogs with one volume request per metric query cache miss, sent next to the query and bounded by it
limits.error: none; a failed or cancelled volume request leaves the estimate
limits.loki_parity: data.stats.summary.totalBytesProcessed of Loki's metric queries
limits.sizing: Off by default: reading the line bytes of a selector costs VictoriaLogs about six times a count over the same window (24h of every stream on the test stack: 0.55 s against 0.09 s), on every metric query cache miss. Turn it on only where exact bytes in Grafana's inspector are worth that VictoriaLogs time; the volume caches answer repeats.

limits.bounds: false (the default) estimates a log query's lines processed from its answer; true counts them with VictoriaLogs, one timestamp-only count request of the query's stream selector over the 1h pieces Loki reads, per log query cache miss that fills its limit or filters lines, sent after the answer and bounded by the request
limits.error: none; a failed or cancelled count leaves the estimate
limits.metric: loki_vl_proxy_backend_read_bytes_total{kind="raw"} counts the extra requests' bytes (one row each)
limits.loki_parity: data.stats.summary.totalLinesProcessed of Loki's log queries
limits.sizing: Off by default: the count reads only the timestamps of the selector's streams over the pieces read (about a volume query's VictoriaLogs time; 24h of every stream on the test stack: 0.09 s), but it is one more VictoriaLogs request for every log query cache miss on every replica, which a fleet multiplies by its replicas and clients. Turn it on where exact lines processed in Grafana's inspector are worth that load; repeats are cache hits and send none.

limits.bounds: how a row whose _msg is VictoriaLogs' missing-message placeholder (its -defaultMsgValue, or -backend-default-msg-value) is read: a JSON line pushed to VictoriaLogs' Loki push route without disable_message_parsing=1, which VictoriaLogs stores as one field per key. false (the default) reports every stored field of such a row as structured metadata (parsed labels after | json or | logfmt); true reads every one as a key of the row's JSON line, as Loki holds the pushed line: no label until | json or a json extraction list reads it, none from | logfmt (an extraction list's names empty), and a query whose every log selector reads a label no stage can give such a line (an unwrap, or a label filter an empty value fails, after | logfmt or without a parser) leaves those rows out with one extra_filters filter on the rows' stored _msg, which VictoriaLogs evaluates before the query's pipes. Nothing grows with the setting: the reading is per row, from the fields VictoriaLogs already returns
limits.error: none; with true, structured metadata pushed beside such a line is hidden, because VictoriaLogs stores it among the line's keys and cannot tell them apart, and so are the fields of every other row VictoriaLogs stored without a message (jsonline rows and OpenTelemetry map bodies without one, attributes included). It acts in the Loki-compatible profile only (-label-style=underscores, -metadata-field-mode=translated, the defaults)
limits.loki_parity: the labels and samples Loki's pipeline takes from a pushed JSON line (profiles/json-line-stored-without-line)
limits.sizing: Off by default: the supported setup is to push JSON lines with disable_message_parsing=1 (or start VictoriaLogs with -loki.disableMessageParsing), which keeps the line and needs no flag. Turn it on only where JSON lines already reach VictoriaLogs' Loki push route with message parsing on and carry no structured metadata, for example Promtail or Alloy pushes of JSON logs, and no jsonline or OpenTelemetry rows without a message carry fields that must stay visible. VictoriaLogs must keep a non-empty -defaultMsgValue (its default), and a customized one is named with -backend-default-msg-value. Its VictoriaLogs cost is one exact match on _msg for the queries it restricts, measured in the pull request that added it; with the flag off the proxy sends exactly what it sent before. Line filters (|= and |~), label filters an empty value passes before any parser, and | logfmt grouping keys still read what VictoriaLogs stored (docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md).

limits.bounds: the default number of log lines per query when the client sends no limit
limits.error: none
limits.loki_parity: Loki's default limit of a log query (100); Grafana sends its Max lines (1000) as the limit
limits.sizing: Raise it only with -max-entries-limit-per-query; every line is transferred and rendered.
